definition: Capabilities serving both beneficial and harmful ends: the same model that explains biology can assist misuse; the same voice cloning that dubs films enables fraud.
details: Capabilities serving both beneficial and harmful ends: the same model that explains biology can assist misuse; the same voice cloning that dubs films enables fraud. Frontier-model release decisions and safety frameworks (responsible scaling policies, preparedness evaluations) are structured around dual-use capability thresholds.

explainer.lead: Dual-use describes a capability that can help people and also enable harm. It matters because judging only the intended, beneficial use can miss risks that should shape evaluations and release decisions.

tiers.eli5: A kitchen knife can help cook dinner, but it can also hurt someone. A powerful AI skill can work the same way: teaching biology is helpful, while the same skill might help someone misuse that knowledge. People check what it can do before sharing it widely.
tiers.practitioner: Apply the idea during capability assessment and release planning: identify beneficial uses, plausible harmful uses, and whether observed capabilities cross thresholds in a responsible scaling policy or preparedness evaluation. Avoid treating a demonstration, a benign primary use case, or good intentions as proof that misuse is impossible.
tiers.paperLevel: A capability C is dual-use when applications G and H both depend on C, where G provides a benefit and H enables harm. Governance can therefore evaluate capability thresholds rather than intent alone, although the dual-use label itself neither quantifies risk nor determines whether a release is safe.

explainer.example: A voice-cloning system can dub an actor’s lines into another language for a film. The same generated voice could imitate that actor in a phone call to trick someone into sending money, so a release review must consider both uses.

usedIn.name: Frontier-model release decisions
usedIn.detail: Reviews consider whether the same capabilities that support valuable applications could also assist misuse.

usedIn.name: Responsible scaling policies
usedIn.detail: Dual-use capability thresholds help structure decisions as models become more capable.

usedIn.name: Preparedness evaluations
usedIn.detail: Evaluations examine potentially harmful capabilities alongside their beneficial applications.

explainer.intuition: The benefit and the danger can come from exactly the same underlying capability, not from two separate technologies. Assessing only what a model is meant to do therefore gives an incomplete picture of what it enables.
howItWorks: Identify the underlying capability rather than only the product’s intended purpose.
Map both beneficial applications and plausible harmful applications of that capability.
Evaluate whether the capability crosses thresholds used in safety frameworks.
Use the findings to inform preparedness work and frontier-model release decisions.
explainer.whyItMatters: Dual-use analysis makes harmful applications visible before a capability is released or scaled. It gives safety frameworks a way to connect observed capabilities with concrete thresholds and release decisions.
misconceptions: Dual-use does not mean every beneficial capability is automatically too dangerous to release.
Good intentions or a helpful primary use do not eliminate the possibility of harmful use.
